title: Chapter 271: Are You There? [2 in 1]
html:
After repairing the door and lock, Chen Ge and Xiao Gu dragged the Ghost Stories Society members to the first floor and secured them inside the dressing room.

“Boss, are you sure this is safe?” Xiao Gu tested the lock. “Should I fetch some rope and tie them up?”

Chen Ge saw clear progress in Gu Feiyu. He removed his costume and handed it over. “That won’t be necessary. Put this on and return to the third floor. Visitors are waiting.”

“No problem. Leave it to me.” This time, Xiao Gu donned Doctor Skull-cracker’s uniform without hesitation. His enthusiasm was so intense that Chen Ge briefly wondered whether one of the Ghost Stories Society’s monsters had possessed him. He seemed completely different from the reluctant young man of that morning.

“Strange. This morning, entering the Haunted House looked like a march to your execution. What changed?”

“Changed?” Xiao Gu scratched his head, an incongruous gesture in Doctor Skull-cracker’s costume. “I thought the Haunted House existed only to terrify people half to death. I didn’t approve of earning money that way. But after watching you help that couple, I realized our Haunted House can be rather heartwarming.”

“You’ve misunderstood our purpose. Fear strips away the masks people wear each day. In here, no one needs to guard every action or calculate how others see them. They need only scream,” Chen Ge said solemnly. “Modern life creates enormous pressure. This city needs somewhere people can release it freely. You thought we took money merely to frighten them, but in truth, we add a little color to otherwise ordinary lives.”

Chen Ge patted Gu Feiyu’s shoulder, his smile as warm as sunrise. “Do your best to frighten them. That couple is the perfect example. People often forget what they possess; only in deepest despair do they remember what matters most.”

“You’re right!” Gu Feiyu nodded vigorously. His work suddenly seemed almost sacred. “I’ll give this job everything I have!”

“Good luck.” Gu Feiyu’s eagerness reassured Chen Ge. “That’s the proper spirit. Also, set my number as your first speed dial. If anything happens inside the Haunted House that you cannot handle, call me immediately.”

“All right.” To Chen Ge, the arguing couple had been a minor interruption. He had not expected the incident to win Gu Feiyu’s approval—though what the young man admired was the Haunted House that ‘Boss Chen’ had constructed in his imagination.

Chen Ge pushed through the thick curtain. Visitors packed the rest tent, and the promotion had exceeded every expectation. Those unwilling to wait tried other attractions, filling the park with crowds for the first time in years. Though far from New Century Park’s peak, the renewed activity delighted its employees. They finally had work to occupy them; after nearly a decade, the park had come alive again.

After losing two members, the Ghost Stories Society sent no further probes. Perhaps it had recognized the problem: at this rate, testing Chen Ge’s Haunted House would exhaust its membership within days. The crowd still bustled outside at 6:30 p.m., but for safety, Chen Ge stopped admitting visitors. Employees began cleaning, and by seven, the park was emptying.

The day’s attendance broke New Century Park’s six-month record. Director Luo had called Uncle Xu away during lunch, apparently to discuss the promotion’s next phase. “Thank you for your help today!”

Once the gates closed, Chen Ge counted the day’s revenue. Cash and electronic payments totaled nearly 15,000—less than he had expected, largely because safety required strict capacity limits. Minghun admitted four visitors at most; Murder by Midnight, seven. Demand had pushed Mu Yang High School’s limit to twelve. The first two scenarios took roughly twenty minutes per group, while even a twelve-person tour of Mu Yang High School lasted forty.

Revenue grew slowly, but the Haunted House’s reputation soared. More visitors promoted it voluntarily to friends and family, both in person and through social media.

It was a virtuous cycle. An ordinary Haunted House lost visitors once its limited sets became familiar. Chen Ge’s scenarios, however, were divided by difficulty. As long as he continued adding newer, scarier challenges, attendance would grow. Lasting goodwill mattered far more than immediate profit.

Only one group found eighteen name tags all day. It included students from Jiujiang Medical University who had arrived with Yang Chen and several repeat visitors. When Chen Ge invited them to try the neighboring scenario, every battered-looking member refused with absolute conviction.

At last, the working day ended. After Xu Wan and Xiao Gu departed, Chen Ge transferred bonuses into their accounts. Once the remaining tasks were finished, he opened the dressing room. Wei Wu and Kong Xiangming were awake.

The loss of their possessing monsters had severely damaged their minds. Both looked vacant and confused, as though their memories had vanished. Chen Ge led them outside and personally delivered them to Captain Yan at the police station.

…

Xiao Gu wandered aimlessly along the road, repeatedly touching his face. After spending an entire day behind the strange mask, he could still feel it clinging to his skin.

Where will I sleep tonight? After that fight with Manager Huang, returning to the security dormitory seems unwise. Brother Chen has already helped me so much. I can’t ask for an advance.

He shoved his hands into his pockets. As he searched desperately for a solution, a bank notification arrived.

Brother Chen has given me a bonus? But it’s only my first day.

The message showed an 800 deposit—enough to rent a comfortable room in Western Jiujiang. Compared with his treatment by the security company, the gesture moved Xiao Gu deeply. Boss Chen is truly a good man!

Pocketing his phone, Xiao Gu headed to the security dormitory at Fang Hwa Apartments. He would pack tonight and find his own room the next day. He arrived around eight and found Manager Huang waiting with a sour expression.

“Where have you been?” The man wore a tailored suit and spotless suede shoes. Manager Huang always seemed to have some grievance against Gu Feiyu.

“I was looking for you. I found another job, so I’ll move out tomorrow.” Gu Feiyu was blunt by nature and said exactly what he thought. Uncle Wong hurried from the bedroom and tugged his sleeve, then bowed apologetically to Manager Huang. “Please forgive him. Xiao Gu is young and speaks too directly.”

He turned and glared at Gu Feiyu. “Why can’t you control that temper of yours?”

“No need for him to change. This place is too small for such a grand personality.” Manager Huang placed a form on the table. “Even if you weren’t quitting, I would dismiss you. Complete this, and be gone by tomorrow.”

Manager Huang pushed Uncle Wong aside and stopped at the doorway. “One more thing. You recommended him, Uncle Wong, so the cost of the damage and his medical expenses will come from your wages.”

“What does any of that have to do with Uncle Wong? Deduct it from my pay.” Xiao Gu struggled to remain calm.

“Your pay? The contract was explicit: wages accrue only after a full month. You’re leaving early. Did you think the contract meant nothing? Consider how much trouble you’ve caused in less than a month.” Manager Huang walked away without looking back. “You expect a salary? Dream on!”

Gu Feiyu lunged forward, ready to beat the man senseless, but Uncle Wong restrained him. “Xiao Gu, don’t be reckless. Be patient.”

“Uncle, I can accept losing my wages, but I won’t let him deduct those expenses from yours!”

“You’re a grown man. Why are you still so impulsive?” Uncle Wong made Gu Feiyu sit, then closed the bedroom door. “Jobs are difficult to find. Tell me about this new position. If the conditions are good, perhaps I’ll join you.”

Uncle Wong feared that Gu Feiyu had been deceived and used the question to learn more. Mentioning the new job calmed the young man slightly. “I work at a Haunted House, frightening visitors. The boss is wonderful. Today was my first shift, and he already gave me a bonus.”

“Is that so?” Uncle Wong remained suspicious. “You trust too easily. Even when working for someone else, protect yourself. Don’t cause trouble, but beware of people who might cheat you.”

“I’ll be fine, Uncle.”

Still worried, Uncle Wong offered advice until 8:30 p.m., then changed into his security uniform and prepared to leave.

“Uncle, I remember you had the morning shift today, right? Where are you going so late at night?”

“Since the murderer was discovered here, everyone has been uneasy. Management requires at least two guards overnight.”

“Let me take your shift tonight.” Xiao Gu felt guilty; Uncle Wong’s wages would not have been docked without him.

“Rest well so you have energy for work tomorrow.” Thermos in hand, Uncle Wong left the room, then turned back at the door. “If the new job doesn’t suit you, call me. I still have connections here.”

“Don’t worry. However tiring it is, the new job is still better than security work.”

“You cheeky brat.” Uncle Wong shook his head and finally departed.

He walked slowly to Fang Hwa Apartments’ rear gate. After speaking with the guard he was relieving, he took the post alone. Two officers worked nights—one at the front gate and one at the rear—so they seldom saw each other.

As night deepened, the usually deserted rear gate grew even more desolate. A murderer had recently infiltrated the complex, so Uncle Wong remained vigilant, repeatedly checking the entrance from his seat beside the window. But after working all morning, age and exhaustion soon pulled his head down to the desk.

Around eleven, the phone on his desk rang and jolted Uncle Wong awake. Gripping his imitation police baton, he surveyed the room and the dim street outside. No one was there.

Phew, scared me.

Uncle Wong sipped from his thermos and checked the phone. A WeChat message awaited him.

“Are you there?”

Uncle Wong rarely used social media and stared in confusion. Who sent this?

The sender’s profile was private and visible only to friends. Uncle Wong studied the name and picture but could not remember adding the person. Aside from family and colleagues, only residents of this complex know my WeChat account.

Uncle Wong searched his memory without success, though the profile seemed vaguely familiar. He considered a voice reply but decided that one might be impolite so late at night. Instead, he slowly typed, “Yes. How can I help?”

Several seconds later, the reply came.

“I live on the twenty-third floor of Building Three. Something is wrong with the family across the hall. Their children won’t stop crying, but I cannot hear any adults. Please send someone quickly.”

Crying children? The twenty-third floor of Building Three?Uncle Wong assumed the sender was a resident. Similar complaints had occurred before.

“All right. I’ll be there shortly.” As a precaution, Uncle Wong messaged the guard at the front gate, then called Manager Huang. No one answered.

Why is it the third building again? So many things are happening here.

Uncle Wong took his baton and hurried to Building Three. He knew the rumors surrounding its elevator, but climbing twenty-three floors would take too long in an emergency.

I should wait for Uncle Wei before taking the elevator.Uncle Wong remained in the lobby, but his phone soon rang again.

“Are you there?”

“Yes.”

“The children are crying even harder. Something is wrong! Where are you people?”

Reading the message, Uncle Wong pressed the elevator button. To his surprise, the car was already waiting on the first floor. “I’m coming. Don’t worry.”

As the silver-gray doors closed, Uncle Wong’s heart quickened. The confined space made breathing difficult. The display soon reached twenty-three, and the doors opened upon an unnaturally silent corridor. Uncle Wong stepped out carefully and switched on his flashlight, but its narrow beam offered no comfort. It only sharpened his unease.

“I’m on the twenty-third floor. What is your room number?”

“3239.”

Swallowing hard, Uncle Wong crept into the darkness, illuminating each number with his flashlight. The corridor seemed endless before he finally found Room 3239.

There’s no crying.He listened outside Room 3239, but silence filled the apartment. Is this a prank, or has something already happened?

Uncertain, Uncle Wong took out his phone to question the sender. Another message arrived first.

“Are you there?”

“I’m outside Room 3239, but I hear nothing. Did you give me the wrong number?” Typing was too slow, so Uncle Wong sent a voice message. A moment later, his recorded voice played behind him.

“Who’s there?”

Uncle Wong slowly turned. The door opposite Room 3239 stood slightly ajar, and a deathly pale figure crouched in the gap, holding a phone.

…

At 11:15 p.m., just as Xiao Gu prepared to sleep, his phone vibrated. The message came from Uncle Wong and contained only three words.

“Are you there?”
